title: Zhuangzi · The Inner Chapters
entry: A butterfly dream, Cook Ding’s practiced movement, and the fasting of the heart-mind.
depth: Perspective, transformation and the limits of fixed judgments. The stories make difficult philosophy available through concrete scenes.
selection: The seven Inner Chapters. Robert Eno’s university-hosted translation supplies an accessible starting edition; compare translation choices before adoption.

title: Dhammapada · Sayings of the Dhamma
entry: Brief verses describe an unsettled mind and the work of cultivating it.
depth: Attention, desire, conduct and liberation. Read mental training within the work’s Buddhist purposes.
selection: The complete short verse collection, with close reading of the opening and Cittavagga, verses 33–43. Proposed translation: Bhikkhu Sujato.

title: Al-Ghazālī · Deliverance from Error
entry: A scholar’s confidence in what he knows gives way to searching doubt.
depth: Perception, reason, certainty and Sufi practice. A Persian author writing in Arabic develops an account that deserves study on its own terms.
selection: The complete short work. Select a modern scholarly translation; the linked historical version enables an initial comparison.

title: René Descartes · Meditations on First Philosophy
form: Early modern European philosophy, written in Latin
entry: Dreaming and doubt unsettle ordinary certainty; the thinker examines what remains.
depth: The thinking self, knowledge and embodiment. Compare the argument with al-Ghazālī without assuming either agreement or direct influence.
selection: Meditations I, II and VI, with a short guide to III–V. The complete six meditations remain available for deeper reading.

title: W. E. B. Du Bois · The Souls of Black Folk
form: African American essays, history and music
entry: A person encounters the self through other people’s racialized judgments.
depth: Double-consciousness, social recognition and the relation between inward life and public power. The Sorrow Songs make listening central.
selection: Forethought and chapters I, III, XI, XIII and XIV. Retain the musical epigraphs and pair chapter XIV with historically contextualized recordings selected with music faculty.

title: Natsume Sōseki · Kokoro
entry: A young man tries to understand the private life of a person he calls Sensei.
depth: Heart, mind, secrecy and responsibility. Narrative makes knowing another person a different undertaking from explaining a mechanism.
selection: The complete novel over three weeks. Confirm the translation and divide readings by that edition. Its extended narrative gives the course time to develop and revise interpretations.
